definition: a wealthy and powerful person in business or industry
hook: Tycoon was a title invented to impress foreigners, and it worked on the Americans.
modernAnchor: A corner office, a private jet, a name on the side of a tower. We call that person a tycoon.
journey: Japan was ruled by the shogun, but shogun only meant general. For dealing with foreign powers, his court wanted something grander.
So in letters abroad he was styled taikun, the great lord. When Commodore Perry arrived in 1853, that was the title he was given.
Americans carried the word home. Abraham Lincoln's own secretaries used it as their private nickname for him. The Tycoon.
After the First World War, magazines pinned it on the barons of oil, steel and rail. The shogun was gone. The title went to the money.
